newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Morgan Stanley ups Applied.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Morgan Stanley ups Applied.

text.p: -- Morgan Stanley analyst Jay Deahna said he upgraded his rating on Applied Materials Inc to strong buy from outperform, boosted his 12-month target price to $65 from $50 and raised his earnings estimates for the 1997 and 1998 fiscal years.

-- The analyst said he expected Applied, the industry's leading supplier of semiconductor production equipment, to report earnings for the first quarter ended in January "in line with or slightly better than" his estimate of $0.44 per share, which is also the current Wall Street consensus.
-- The first quarter report is due out next Tuesday.

-- Deahna also said he is loooking for first quarter bookings to be better than expected. In a previous conference call, the company had indicated it expected bookings of $700 to $750 million, but "I think its going to be higher than $750 (million)," the Morgan Stanley analyst said.

-- Deahna said he likes Applied because of its broad global infrastructure, its strategic relationship as a supplier to virtually every major semiconductor manufacturer and its broad and expanding product line.

-- "Applied is one of three equipment suppliers that sells equipment into just about every chip maker," he said. The other two are KLA Instruments Corp and Tencor Instruments, which last month agreed to merge.

-- The company is getting a very good share of the contracts from both high volume strategic fabrication plants and in pilot lines, the plants where leading edge technology under 0.25 microns in size are produced.
-- The analyst said he believes Applied is using its various strengths to gain market share during the current industry slump, continuing its pattern of outpacing industry growth rates.

-- In light of the current downturn, he said he expected Applied revenues to shrink eight percent in 1997 compared with an industry decline of 16 percent or so. As the pace picks up again in 1998, he said he expected Applied to grow 18 percent verus the industry growth of 10 to 15 percent.
